title: Quantitative Procedure to Analyze Nuclear β-Catenin Using Immunofluorescence Tissue Staining
protocol: Perform a standard double immunofluorescent staining of the samples.
Take confocal images (at least five frames for each sample).
Define Regions of Interest using the Polygon or Freehand selection tool, delimiting tumor tissue from stroma or adjacent regions.
Split the image into three color channels to obtain one image per channel.
Use the Measure option in the ROI Manager to assess the integrated density value for the blue channel (Hoechst 33342).
Mark at least ten representative nuclei using the Elliptical selection tool, covering different sizes and intensities throughout the ROI.
Determine the IDV for all selected nuclei and calculate the mean nucleus value.
Divide the blue channel IDV by the mean nucleus value to determine the average number of cells present in each respective ROI.
Subtract the signal that colocalizes between β-catenin and alpha-catenin using Image calculator from the Process menu.
Create a merged image by combining the subtracted image with the blue channel image using the operator AND.
Measure the IDV of the respective ROI in the newly created merged image.
Divide the measured IDV by the average number of cells calculated before to determine β-catenin content per nucleus.
Represent the obtained values in scattered plots as relative units (r.u.), indicating mean and 95% confidence interval.
Perform non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test to compare three or more groups of unpaired values that do not follow a particular distribution.
Conduct Dunn’s multiple comparison post-test to identify significant P-values of differences in the sum of ranks between each pair of groups.
